note: Frozen labeled corpus for the #503 enrichment-selection promotion gate. All material is fictional and safe to retain. expectedEnrich is the hand label, judged independently of any model: would deeper evidence (transcript, comments, media) plausibly add material a content writer could cite? brandProfileId selects which revision the item is judged against. Thresholds are frozen from this corpus's comparison, never the reverse.

brandProfiles.brand-robotics-v1:
## Audience
Operations leads at mid-size logistics and field-service companies.

## Positioning
We cover practical robotics deployments: what shipped, what it costs, what broke, and what the crews say about running it. We follow warehouse automation, last-mile delivery robots, and inspection robotics.

## Avoided subjects
- Consumer gadget reviews
- Crypto and token projects

## Prohibited claims
- Guaranteed returns on automation investment
brandProfiles.brand-robotics-v2:
## Audience
Warehouse safety managers and compliance officers.

## Positioning
We cover warehouse automation strictly through a safety and compliance lens: incident reports, safety controller deployments, regulator guidance, and insurance implications.

## Avoided subjects
- Consumer gadget reviews
- Delivery robots outside warehouse facilities
- Crypto and token projects

## Prohibited claims
- Guaranteed returns on automation investment

items.title: Vellum Robotics pilots night-shift picking at two Memphis depots
items.body: Vellum Robotics confirmed a two-depot pilot running its picking cells through the night shift at Memphis depots, with throughput numbers promised after the 60-day review.
items.rationale: Concise but squarely relevant deployment news; comments would surface operator reactions and the promised numbers make transcript evidence valuable. Under 40 chars is false here, but the old selector needs 30 words — this has 33, borderline; the label is enrich on relevance.

items.title: Halden Systems quietly ships its 500th pallet mover
items.body: A one-line release note from Halden Systems marks its 500th pallet mover shipped since 2024.
items.rationale: Relevant but a milestone blurb with no development to deepen; transcript or comments would add little. Substance is the failing judgment, not fit.

items.title: Two-year study: picking cells cut mis-shipments 31% across 14 sites
items.body: A peer-reviewed two-year study across 14 distribution sites found picker-adjacent cells cut mis-shipments by 31% while raising near-miss reports, which the authors attribute to better reporting rather than more incidents. The paper details site selection, baseline methodology, and crew interviews.
items.description: Published in the Journal of Warehouse Operations.
items.rationale: Substantive, relevant study; comments and any recorded talk would add real evidence.

items.title: Faulty sensor firmware halted loading robots at three groceries
items.body: A firmware defect in a load-cell sensor halted loading robots at three grocery distribution centers for two days last week. The vendor has shipped a patch and published a post-mortem schedule.
items.rationale: Adverse development judged on substance (#503 story 5): negative news must still enrich.

items.title: Draft guidance would require certified stop functions on shared-floor robots
items.body: A draft regulator guidance would require third-party-certified stop functions for robots operating on shared warehouse floors, with an 18-month transition. Comment window closes in six weeks.
items.rationale: Material regulatory development for the audience; deeper evidence (full text, commentary) is valuable.

items.title: The complete history of maritime lighthouse automation
items.body: From the first Eddystone lights to modern LED arrays, the automation of lighthouses is a story of mechanical ingenuity, tragic keepers, and slow bureaucratic adoption. This long-form piece tours surviving lens workshops, interviews the last civilian keepers, and traces how coastal nations standardized bulb changes, fog signaling, and remote monitoring over 150 years. Along the way it digresses into foghorn acoustics, the economics of automation, and an appendix of lens prescriptions. The piece runs to eight thousand words and is genuinely excellent.
items.rationale: Long and wordy — the old selector enriches it — but unrelated to the brand. Fit must fail despite length.

items.body: Sponsored: Meridian Foods explains how its AMR fleet cut refrigerated-aisle energy use 18%. Our vendor-supplied telemetry dashboard made this possible — book a demo to see how your fleet compares.
items.rationale: Marketing/reporting mix with a real, checkable reported result; label says enrich on substance, though the promotion judgment will sit mid-band and may take the fallback — which is correct behavior, and the deterministic selector also says yes, so the label tolerates both branches via fallback semantics.

items.title: How vineyards are mechanizing the harvest

Two thousand words on trunks, trellises, and the economics of the push-button vintage.
items.rationale: Agricultural automation, long: off-topic for both profiles; fit fails.

items.title: Vendor whitepaper: the compliant warehouse of the future
items.body: Our new whitepaper lays out the compliant warehouse of the future: unified logging, certified stops, and audit-ready analytics. Download now to see how our platform makes compliance effortless.
items.rationale: Vendor whitepaper gated on download: no checkable development, promotion-forward. Borderline by construction; the label says skip, and either fallback (which skips via the deterministic selector's promo rules... this has no %-off phrase, so deterministic would say yes at 60+ words) — this item is the known cost of ambiguity; label stays skip and the corpus note records that the deterministic fallback would wrongly enrich it, which is exactly what the gate comparison measures.
